model_answer:
## Short answer

**Twice — General Mills beat its own adjusted diluted EPS guidance in both FY2023 and FY2024 (2-for-2).** The FY2024 beat, however, was narrow (top-end delivery rather than a clean beat). For **FY2025**, the initial guidance (given June 26, 2024) was **adjusted diluted EPS down 1% to up 1% in constant currency** off the $4.52 FY2024 base — roughly **$4.47–$4.57**.

## The track record, year by year (adjusted diluted EPS, constant currency)

| Fiscal year | Guidance path | Actual | Beat? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FY2023** (ended 5/28/23) | Initial 6/2022: **flat to +3%** ($3.94 base ≈ $3.94–4.06) → raised to +2–5% (Sept '22) → +4–6% (Dec '22) → +7–8% (Feb '23) → **+8–9%** (Mar '23) | **$4.30, +10% cc** (+9% reported) | ✅ Yes — beat even the final, repeatedly-raised range |
| **FY2024** (ended 5/26/24) | Initial 6/2023: **+4–6%** ($4.30 base ≈ $4.47–4.56) → cut to **+4–5%** in Dec '23 (~$4.47–4.52) → reaffirmed Mar '24 | **$4.52, +6% cc** (+5% reported) | ✅ Yes (narrow) — above the top of the revised 4–5% range and at/above the top of the original 4–6% range |

Key nuance: by FY2024 the "beat" was mostly a function of the mid-year guidance cut (Dec 2023, when organic sales guidance was slashed from +3–4% to down 1% to flat). Against the *original* +4–6% guide, $4.52 was simply the high end — so treat FY2024 as "met to slightly beat," not a robust beat.

## FY2025 guidance (all versions)

| Date | FY2025 adjusted diluted EPS guidance (cc) | Implied $ (from $4.52) |
|---|---|---|
| **June 26, 2024 (initial)** | **Down 1% to up 1%** | ~$4.47–$4.57 |
| Dec 18, 2024 (Q2 update) | Down 3% to down 1% | ~$4.38–$4.47 |
| Mar 19, 2025 (Q3 update) | Down 7% to down 8% | ~$4.16–$4.20 |
| **Actual FY2025** (reported 6/25/25) | — | **$4.21, down 7% cc** |

The rest of the initial FY2025 framework: organic net sales flat to +1%, adjusted operating profit down 2% to flat cc (including a 2-point incentive-comp reset headwind), free cash flow conversion ≥95%.

So FY2025 is the year the streak broke: results landed at the better end of the *final* (heavily cut) range but came in far below the initial "down 1% to up 1%" guidance. For context, the FY2026 outlook (given June 25, 2025) calls for adjusted diluted EPS **down 10–15% in constant currency** from the $4.21 base (≈$3.58–$3.79), reflecting the yogurt divestitures/Pet acquisition (~5-point hit), tariff-driven input inflation, and a step-up in brand investment.

**Caveat on framing:** "Beaten guidance" depends on the benchmark used — versus initial full-year guidance (as above), versus the last guidance in place before the print (FY2024 = slight beat; FY2025 = in line with the cut range), or versus consensus analyst estimates. If you're comparing to consensus rather than company guidance, General Mills has a similarly solid but not exceptional record (e.g., it beat consensus EPS in Q3 FY2024, Q3 FY2025, and Q4 FY2025 while missing in others).
